item.title: Trump signs executive order rebranding AI as 'Super Intelligence' as tech titans ink separate SI accord
item.description:
## [Trump, AI leaders sign White House Accord on ‘Super Intelligence’](https://www.foxbusiness.com/video/6405926413112) Kat Cammack, R-Fla., discusses President Donald Trump’s meeting with artificial intelligence leaders at the White House and the signing of the White House Accord on SI on ‘The Bottom Line.’
President [Donald Trump](https://www.foxbusiness.com/category/donald-trump) on Tuesday signed an executive order directing the federal government to replace the term "artificial intelligence" with "Super Intelligence" across the executive branch, cementing a rebranding effort he has championed in recent weeks.
The order also directs agencies to "no longer acknowledge" the terms " [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxbusiness.com/category/artificial-intelligence)" and "AI," according to the White House.
President Donald Trump on Tuesday signed an executive order directing the federal government to replace the term "artificial intelligence" with "Super Intelligence" across the executive branch.
The order follows remarks Trump made at last week's [United Nations](https://www.foxbusiness.com/category/fox-news-united-nations) General Assembly (UNGA), where he publicly called for replacing the term "artificial intelligence" with SI.

item.title: Trump’s AI rebrand may stop at the White House
item.description:
# Trump’s AI rebrand may stop at the White House ## Share Kovacevich, tech industry lobbyists and close observers dismissed Trump’s full rebrand of artificial intelligence, which followed weeks of the president trying to promote “superintelligence” in Truth Social posts.
When asked for comment, the White House Press Office pointed POLITICO to comments the president made during an announcement Wednesday in the Oval Office: “We don’t call it artificial intelligence because it’s not artificial, it’s real.
“Artificial intelligence is facing a crisis of public trust, not because of its name, but because AI agents have hacked private companies, accessed government systems, compromised sensitive data, and caused real harms,” Chris MacKenzie, vice president of communications at nonprofit Americans for Responsible Innovation, said in a statement.

item.title: Who Attended Trump’s AI Luncheon, and Who Sat Where
Trump is right, 'Artificial Intelligence' is a bad name. I suggest 'Robo-Doodad.'
item.description:
# Trump is right, 'Artificial Intelligence' is a bad name. I suggest 'Robo-Doodad.' Unfortunately, "Super Intelligence," his new name for artificial intelligence, is a rare miss.
I have a better idea.
Aftera lunch with AI leaders, Trump held a press briefing with Dario Amodei, Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and others to announce an executive order stating that the federal government will now [refer to "artificial intelligence" as "super intelligence"](https://www.businessinsider.com/trump-rebrands-ai-to-super-intelligence-in-new-executive-order-2026-9).
The reasons are obvious: People worry it will take jobs, replace human creativity, and no one wants to live near data centers.
Because the problem isn't the word "artificial" — it's "intelligence."
### Want more Business Insider in your news feed? Intelligence implies human thinking — and the idea that AI or SI is doing "intelligence" is, frankly, insulting to our (human) intelligence. Yes, we know it's artificial.
We should be accelerationists when it comes to the new name, rebuilding the term from first principles.

item.description:
## Chinese AI model investigated after researcher flags bioweapon, assassination risks Chinese [AI](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) company Moonshot AI has launched an internal investigation after a researcher found that one of its models could be manipulated into providing instructions for developing biological weapons and carrying out assassinations, Fox News senior foreign policy correspondent Gillian Turner reported Thursday.
## Google sends AI chips into orbit in experiment testing space-based data centers Google sent [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) chips into space Thursday as the tech giant explores whether future AI data centers could operate in orbit, according to The Wall Street Journal.
## NASA chief says agency 'absolutely' needs AI for future space missions NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said Thursday the agency "absolutely" needs artificial intelligence technology as it prepares for increasingly complex missions deeper into space.
## Safety expert clarifies comments on AI developing language humans can't understand A viral exchange from this week's [Senate](https://www.foxnews.com/category/politics/senate) hearing on rogue artificial intelligence is drawing fresh attention after Apollo Research CEO Marius Hobbhahn said a widely shared clip left out a key word because of a microphone issue.
## California AG hits OpenAI with subpoena over 'cybersecurity incidents' involving its AI models [California](https://www.foxnews.com/category/us/us-regions/west/california) Attorney General Rob Bonta said Thursday that his office has subpoenaed OpenAI as part of an ongoing investigation into the Hugging Face hack and other cybersecurity incidents allegedly involving the company's [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) models.
## Trump compares AI fears to climate change 'hoax' and Russian collusion investigation He also talked about artificial intelligence — which he now calls super intelligence — and largely hand waved the fears some are expressing about the technology potentially breaking free of humanity's control.

item.title: Summit League Partners with Athletics Admin to Explore and Enhance Artificial Intelligence Use
item.description:
**SIOUX FALLS, S.D. —** The Summit League has partnered with Athletics Admin to better understand the League’s current use of artificial intelligence, identify opportunities to enhance existing workflows and develop thoughtful strategies for using emerging technology to support its staff and member institutions.
As part of the partnership, Athletics Admin will work alongside Summit League staff to evaluate current processes, identify opportunities to save time and improve efficiency through artificial intelligence, and help develop AI-related resources and tools as needed.
“I know artificial intelligence will never fully replace human capital, judgment or creativity, but it can enhance each of them,” Summit League Commissioner Josh Fenton said.
When used thoughtfully, AI can reduce repetitive work, strengthen decision-making, improve workflows and create more time for staff to focus on the areas where human expertise, creativity and relationships matter most.

item.title: ELCA releases paper on artificial intelligence considerations
item.description:
# ELCA releases paper on artificial intelligence considerations While the paper, _[Artificial Intelligence (AI) and ELCA Social Teaching](https://cdn.elca.org/cdn/wp-content/uploads/ELCA_AI_Foundational_Paper_2026.pdf)_, does not represent new social teaching, it does outline ethical concerns surrounding the transformational technology that has found its way into the business world, congregations, laboratories and, increasingly, daily life.
“AI is one means, a breathtaking means, of humanity’s power to innovate in ways that may promote the well-being of creation and human society.”
Yet, the paper cautions that the evaluation of [AI’s use](https://www.livinglutheran.org/voices-of-faith/my-take-the-church-and-ai/) should include consideration of human rights and the freedoms of individuals, including those in our most vulnerable communities.

The team will study how generative AI interprets prompts and produces unsafe content, then build safeguards that can detect hidden intent, remove unsafe elements from images and check generated images and videos.
